paragraphs.text: And so more fit to give counsel than now to act great exploits, εργα νεων, βουλαι δε γερονων. Howbeit he was willing to show that although he was old and withering, yet "the root of the matter was in him"; and like the rose, he kept his sweet savour, though he had lost his lovely colour.
Audite senem iuvenes, quem iuvenem senes audierunt, said old Augustus to his mutineers, and settled them.
paragraphs.anchor: I am old and stricken in age.

paragraphs.text: “ Tanta fuit quondam capitis reverentia cani,
Inque sou precio ruga senilis erat. ”

Joshua intituleth God to all his conquests so did David, and our Richard I. So have we vanquished the king of France at Gisors, said he in his letter to Philip Bishop of Duresme; howbeit, we have not done the same, but Dieu et mon droit God and our right, by us. And the like did our Henry V at the battle of Agincourt; and our late thrice noble generals in their highest achievements at home and abroad. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And ye have seen all that the Lord your God.

paragraphs.text: {a} Hoveden, fol. 445. Speed, 799.
That is, God by my hands, {as Jos 23:3} for he it was who taught mine hands to war, and my fingers to fight.
paragraphs.anchor: With all the nations that I have cut off.

paragraphs.text: The same Hebrew word Jarash here signifieth to possess and to dispossess. Canaanites shall be cast out of what they get or detain from God’s people.
paragraphs.anchor: And drive them from out of your sight; and ye shall possess.

paragraphs.text: Get good store of spiritual mettle, which is got by prayer, and maketh a man invincible. Of cowards they were wont to say in Rome, that there was nothing Roman in them: of many amongst us it may be said, There is nothing Christian in them.

For if ye once give way to come amongst them and converse with them, you will easily and quickly be drawn to do worse; even all that is here mentioned, to make honourable mention of their gods, to swear by them, to serve them, &c. Sin is wondrous catching, and contagious, and Nemo repente fuit turpissimus.
paragraphs.anchor: That ye come not among these nations.

paragraphs.text: viz., Since I have had the governance of you, Vita Principis censura est, imo Cynosura: the life of the prince is the loade star of the Commonwealth, Magnates magnetes; good governors make good people: and on the contrary, Qualis rix, talis grex.
paragraphs.anchor: As ye have done unto this day

paragraphs.text: He hath and he will, if you hinder not your own happiness by breach of covenant.
paragraphs.anchor: For the Lord hath driven out.

paragraphs.text: None of all those who either have assailed you, or have been assaulted by you.
paragraphs.anchor: No man hath been able to stand before you.

paragraphs.text: He who alone is a whole army of men, van and rear, both. {Isa 52:12} He who "strengtheneth" and weakeneth "the arm" of either party, {Eze 30:24} and rendereth their weapons vain or prosperous. {Isa 54:17}
paragraphs.anchor: He it is that fighteth for you.

paragraphs.text: Heb., To your souls, that chief part of yourselves, the welfare whereof lieth upon it.
Apostates cannot choose to themselves a worse condition; there is martial law for such: they "draw back to perdition." {Heb 10:39}
paragraphs.anchor: Else, if ye do in any wise go back.

paragraphs.text: It is not safe to seek the association of others in a sinful way. Jehoshaphat smarted for joining with Ahab: Hunniades, for cleaving to that perjured Popish king at the battle of Varna: the Greek Church, for calling in the help of the Latin Church against the Turk; subjecting themselves to the Bishop of Rome.

As the fowler catcheth birds, and the hunter wild beasts in their snares and traps; so shall these Canaanites catch you by their familiarity and commerce, and draw you to participate in their sins and plagues.
paragraphs.anchor: But they shall be snares and traps unto you.

paragraphs.text: They shall by their injuries vex and disquiet you, they shall with sharpest weapons prick and gore your tenderest parts, without mercy or measure.
paragraphs.anchor: And scourges in your sides, and thorns in your eyes.

paragraphs.text: I am a dying man: and the words of dying men are held to be living oracles: let therefore these last words of mine sink into your souls, and stick by you when I shall go hence and be no more seen. {2Pe 1:13}
paragraphs.anchor: And, behold, this day I am going the way of all the earth.

paragraphs.text: To the sweetness of the promises he fitly adjoineth the tartness of the menaces. Sour and sweet make the best sauce: promises and threatenings mingled serve to keep the heart in the best temper.
paragraphs.anchor: So shall the Lord bring upon you all evil things.

paragraphs.text: This judgment Joshua inculcateth, {Jos 23:13-16} because he knew it would be very grievous to them to forego so goodly a land so lately gotten, and so little a while enjoyed. In the beginning of a speech τα ηθη milder affections suit best; but toward the end thereof τα παθη, saith the orator, passionate and piercing passages. This rule Joshua here observeth, being ex utroque Caesar, no less an orator than a warrior, as hath been already observed.
paragraphs.anchor: And ye shall perish quickly from off the good land.
